pairs.difference: B (scarf with coin): one even, dark line runs around the whole silhouette, from the collar down both tails, and the coin has a doubled ring groove. Outline darkness is 0.038, against 0.003 for A. A (polka-dot bandana): the contour is lighter and drops out along the left fold and the knot, and the only inside edges are the dots.
pairs.fix: Let the scarf's outer edge come from the red cloth meeting the blue background, with no drawn line. Make the edge softer where the cloth folds away from the light, and draw the coin's rim as a thin, crisp step instead of a thick groove.

pairs.difference: B (covered wagon): outline darkness is 0.192, above the real maximum of 0.148. The canvas, the wheel rims and the spokes have heavy, even dark contours. Grass blades and dirt specks fill the foreground with busy edges, as in the generated lighthouse lessons. A (coaster): the edges are strong on the cars and track, and the hills and clouds behind are soft.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark line around the wagon and its wheels; separate them from the scene by color and light only. Paint the dirt road and grass as soft, smooth areas with only a few blades, and keep the crisp edges on the front wheel and the wagon box.

pairs.difference: B (binoculars): each barrel and eyecup ring has a thick, doubled dark contour, and the floorboard gaps are long, hard black lines that compete with the subject. A (cactus): the ribs and spines are fine, the silhouette edge is moderate, and the background stripes are soft.
pairs.fix: Draw the floorboard gaps as faint, soft lines that fade into the distance. Let the edges of the binocular barrels come from the light and dark sides of the green and black parts, without a dark rim line.

pairs.difference: B is the real lighthouse from the lessons: few, clean edges and soft clouds. A (windmill): every blade of the wheel has its own hard outline, which packs the top of the card with edges. The grass at the bottom is a field of sharp, separate strokes.
pairs.fix: Draw the windmill wheel as fewer, broader blades with soft gaps between them. Paint the wheat field as a soft golden mass with only a few blade tips near the tower base.

pairs.difference: A (lasso): edge density inside the subject is 0.271, far above the real maximum of 0.157. Every twist of the rope is drawn as a separate hard edge, so the coils read as dense hatching. B (graduation cap): only the board edge, the band and the tassel carry edges, and the faces are clean.
pairs.fix: Paint the rope as a smooth, rounded tube with a soft, faint twist pattern, sharp only on the side facing the light. Use about half as many twist lines.

pairs.difference: B (pig and cow at a concert): outline darkness is 0.115, above the real maximum of 0.100. The pig, cow, horns and hooves have a dark, even contour, like a sticker outline, and the confetti, light bulbs and stage truss scatter hard edges across the background. A (cowboy and pig): busy, but the background dunes and rocks are soft.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark outline around the pig and the cow. Blur the stage truss, the confetti and the crowd behind them so that the crispest edges stay on the two faces.

pairs.difference: A (scout jacket): edge density inside the subject is 0.159, just above the real maximum. Pockets, flaps, the collar, cuff seams, the sash and four badges, each with an inner pictogram, are all drawn as hard grooves. B (cowboy hat): broad, smooth forms with a single band seam.
pairs.fix: Keep two pockets and the sash, and drop the extra flaps and seams. Draw the remaining seams as thin, shallow creases, not deep grooves. Give the badges simple, bold symbols with no inner rings.

pairs.difference: B (spiral topiary): edge density inside the subject is 0.29, above the real maximum of 0.270. Every leaf has its own hard outline, and the hedge behind is dotted with sharp marks too, so there is no softer area for the eye to rest on. A (mesa): sparse, soft strata lines with one strong contour.
pairs.fix: Paint the topiary tiers as soft, rounded leafy masses, with crisp leaf shapes only along the lit edge of each tier. Make the hedge behind a smooth green band.

pairs.difference: A (popcorn cart): the awning scallops have heavy dark contours, the popcorn piles are a mass of small hard edges, and the paving behind is drawn as a full grid of hard tile lines. B (horseshoe): clean metal edges, crisp nail holes and soft sand, close to the real cards.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark line on the awning edges and let the red and white stripes form the boundary. Paint the popcorn as a soft, lumpy mass, and fade the paving tiles behind the cart.

pairs.difference: A (sneakers): edge density inside the subject is 0.227, the top of the real range, and outline darkness is -0.1, below the real minimum. The mesh dots, lace loops, sole stripes and side panel all have hard edges, and the hard horizon line cuts behind the shoes. B (cowboy boot): stitching is dense, but the leather faces are smooth.
pairs.fix: Paint the mesh fabric as a soft texture with no dot pattern, and reduce the lace crossings. Blur the line where the wall meets the floor.

pairs.difference: A (popsicle): outline darkness is -0.157, far outside the real range. Frost specks and many small droplets scatter hard little edges over the whole bar and its silhouette. B (ring box): has a dark, even contour (0.13, slightly above the real maximum), but its inside is clean, and the medal edge is crisp.
pairs.fix: Draw the popsicle as a smooth, glossy bar with two clean grooves and only three or four droplets near the bitten edge. Leave out the frost speckle.

pairs.difference: B (motel sign): outline darkness is 0.161, above the real maximum of 0.148. The sign boards, arrow and icons have thick double contours, and stars, the balcony rails and the fence add hard edges far from the sign. A (birdhouse): strong edges on the box, with the tree and city behind softer.
pairs.fix: Draw the sign boards with a single crisp rim and no extra dark line around them. Paint the motel building and fence behind as soft, blurred shapes, and leave out the scattered star dots.

pattern: Generated cards put a dark, even line around the whole subject. They also cover the card with small, equally sharp details: rope twists, leaves, mesh, frost, grass blades, tiles. Real cards get their boundaries from color and light, put the crispest edges on the focal object, and leave the background soft.
